posts.title: Reef Log: Dive #142
content: Forty-one minutes at eighteen meters, visibility like tap water for the first time all season.
The octopus that lives by the mooring line was out and unbothered. An entire school of salema parted around us like we were furniture. Logged, grateful.
comments: 142! The mooring-line octopus deserves a name by now.

posts.title: Tide Pools at Low Spring Tide
content: The best diving this week required no tank at all. Spring low tide pulled the water back forty meters and turned the whole shelf into a maze of pools.
Found: three kinds of anemone, one very cross crab, and a sea hare the size of a fist. Lost: one sandal, to the sea, as tribute.

posts.title: The Wreck at 30 Meters
content: First proper deep dive of the year, down the line to the old trawler. Thirty meters is where the colors leave and the calm arrives.
The wreck has more life on it every year — soft corals on the rails, a conger in the engine room, and a cloud of anthias standing guard over the bow.

posts.title: Sea Glass Season
content: Winter storms pay out in spring. The east beach is covered in frosted green and white, with the occasional impossible blue.
The jar on the windowsill is nearly full again. No plans for it. There were never plans for it.

drafts.title: Reef Log: Dive #143
content: Same wall as last week, half the visibility, twice the turtles. Forty minutes at sixteen meters and a very patient buddy.

drafts.title: Gear Check Before the Cold Season
content: The dry suit zipper needs wax and the second regulator needs a service before October. Writing it down so I actually do it.

drafts.title: Night Dive Checklist
content: Two lights, one backup, glow stick on the tank, and a buddy who has done it before. Everything else is optional.
Book the boat for the October full moon dive.
